## Natural history notes

A small fruticose lichen characterized by pale gray-green stalks, or podetia, often tipped with bright red fruiting bodies that give it the “soldier” appearance. In Florida, Southern Soldiers grows on sandy soil, decaying wood, logs, stumps, bark bases, and open disturbed patches in habitats such as pine flatwoods, scrub, sandhills, roadsides, and forest edges. Like other lichens, it is a symbiosis between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, obtaining moisture and nutrients from the air and substrate while helping stabilize soil, colonize bare surfaces, and add texture to dry open microhabitats.
